profile.headline: Software Engineer
profile.summary:
- Software Developer for Schlumberger with the Kinetix Shale Team. 

- Experience developing programs for research purposes including visualization, surface modeling, rendering, and optimization.

- Familiarity with a variety of languages: C++, OpenGL, C,  C#, Latex

- Familiarity with software packages: Mathematica, Maya, Meshlab, Blender, GIMP, Microsoft Visual Studio

- Well-developed oral and written communication skills, as evidence by presentations at national meetings and peer-reviewed publications.

positions.title: Graduate Research Assistant
positions.description:
Research:

- Surface Parameterization research 

Collaboration with the Texas A&M branch of the Gnalić Project:

- Improve reconstruction pipeline of shipwreck excavation

positions.title: Graduate Teaching Assistant
positions.description:
Course:

Computer Graphics

- Core concepts of Computer Graphics using C++, and basic OpenGL usage.
- Held office hours to assist 50-60 Junior - Senior level students on assignments and test preparation

Research:
- Surface Modeling
- Surface Parameterization

positions.title: Graduate Research Assistant
positions.description:
Research supported by DARPA and NSF grants:

- Surface Reconstruction
- Surface and Normal Compression
- Contouring Methods for Discrete Indicator Functions
- Surface Modeling
- Surface Parameterization

Mostly C++ and OpenGL development.  Work with Mathematica and many open source linear solver libraries like TAUCS.

Rendered images for publications, posters, and presentations listed in publications and presentations section using Maya and self made software, as well as images found in the paper "Triangle Surfaces with Discrete Equivalence Classes" http://faculty.cs.tamu.edu/schaefer/research/equivalence.pdf

Motion capture subject for papers: 

- "Leveraging Depth Cameras and Wearable Pressure Sensors for Full-body Kinematics and Dynamics Capture"
- "Accurate Realtime Full-body Motion Capture Using a Single Depth Camera"

positions.title: Research Assistant
positions.description:
Surface Reconstruction and Geometric Compression research:

- Progressive compression of surfaces resulting from progressive surface reconstruction.
- Development of state of the art normal compression method
- C++ and OpenGL development
- Generated test example objects for other related projects as well as rendering figures for papers and presentations with Maya.

positions.title: Undergraduate Summer Research Grant (USRG) Researcher
positions.description:
Progressive Surface Reconstruction research under Dr. Scott Schaefer:

	- Improved speed and quality of existing surface reconstruction system using C++ and OpenGL
	- Generate, clean, and process large 10+ GB data sets
	- Render new images for papers and posters with Maya software

Collaboration with Texas A&M Center for Robot-Assisted Search and Rescue (CRASAR):

        - Process and reconstruct Lidar point cloud data
        - Capturing data sets in real world settings

positions.title: Student Peer Teacher
positions.description:
Course: Introduction to Java

- Basics of Object Oriented programming for beginner and non-major students.
- Java concepts in Linux and Eclipse for Windows
- Assisted running lab for 30-60 students, answering questions, grading, and test study preparation

Course: Honors Data Structures and Algorithms

- C++ STL implementation and analysis for Honors level students
- C++ programming in Linux and Visual Studio for Windows
- Assisted running lab for approximately 30 students, answering questions and test study preperation
